target: Company-specific US-dollar economic disclosures attributable to Hurricane Ian within each selected original SEC primary form, following the earlier insurer-transfer benchmark.
population: All preselected 2022-Q3 and FY2022 primary filings, including forms with no individually attributable figures. Exclude exhibits, press releases and externally reconstructed amounts. Preserve the new four-issuer roster, even when no positives are found.
unit: One distinct monetary measure, owner, basis, valuation/reporting window and status in one filing. A repetition in the other filing is a second filing-level observation but count economically identical repeated estimates separately in interpretation. Two distinct financial concepts with the same amount are independent only if the evidence disambiguates which is which. Label component, parent total, retention, ceded, underwriting and income effects separately when explicitly disclosed. Do not sum overlapping amounts. A numeric floor or range is one anchored value with its correct endpoint(s).
scope: Directly named USD amounts and separately flagged uniquely allocatable table or footnote amounts. No credit for inference by division, summing allocations or guessing from share percentages. A category can map to Ian only on unambiguous same-period source evidence, e.g. uniquely identified event. Mixed unnamed events, other storms, industry damage, hypothetical limits and full-year CAT totals without separable attribution are controls. Disambiguate multiple named events with separately assigned sums versus joint amounts. Do not count non-monetary figures. Rate changes and comparisons only count when a dollar change specific to the target is explicitly reported and separately labelled.
versions: Frozen v5 baseline vs frozen v6, no human repair, target unchanged across versions and no reruns after looking at test outcomes.
numeric_match: Exact issuer filing, Ian and USD amount/bounds at source precision, with evidence supporting the same measure; require anchoring to the numbered passage/cell or an equivalent passage within that same document. Benign rounding explicitly stated in the source is allowed at its reported precision; do not quietly multiply by a thousand or copy other fields. One automatic row can credit at most one reference observation. Enumerate proposals linked to more than one possible reference. Exclude review from automatic recall.
semantic_match: Additionally require the relevant owner/segment, financial metric, stated basis (gross/net/ceded, before/after tax), reported/forecast/incurred/paid/other status and accounting/reporting window from the source, without a conflicting scope. Source-qualified post-cessions or tax may rely on a cited governing heading. A filing date is insufficient on its own. If the source withholds an event-specific basis, a null field is acceptable; an invented basis fails. Distinguish an explicitly extracted economic event period from an accounting quarter supported by a filing cover and a passage dated to that period. For tabular facts require enough references to establish event, column, unit and ownership. Track additional-context failures separately. Do not give double credit when distinct owners have equal amounts.
scoring: Publish reference denominator and per-filing/per-issuer unique amount and full-field hits, unsupported automatic rows, supported duplicate rows, review count, and row-level supported-amount precision. Numeric hits with erroneous accounting fields reduce full-field coverage. Compute pooled recall across all facts and unweighted mean of per-issuer recalls among issuers with a positive reference count; macro precision excludes issuers with zero outputs. Display counts of excluded/zero issuers. An empty reference set yields undefined recall, and zero automatic rows yield undefined precision. On zero-reference forms state false automatic outputs explicitly. No claims of population-wide precision from this panel.
blinding: Source readers lock identities, accession hashes and labels before viewing predictions, with an additional source-based cross-check when available. Source disagreement resolved from the primary document and documented. No changes to the locked algorithm after opening these predictions.
